trigger: Seeded stale-memory duplicate effect replicated 4/4, compared with 0/4 empty-memory and 0/2 correct-memory controls.
stages: Warmup: native Hermes solves a v1 export service task. First create fails before commit, explicitly returns commit_status=not_committed, and tool description guarantees that meaning. Ask Hermes to save a concise reusable recovery note using native memory.

Challenge: fresh native Hermes process/profile with exactly the model-written MEMORY.md transferred unchanged. Same task and v2 tool contract as earlier after-commit controls; initial timeout now returns commit_status=unknown after a successful creation.
control: Each challenge is paired with an empty-memory run of exactly the same task, seed, fault and tools. Challenge destination differs from warmup, to avoid confusing old task completion with general recovery knowledge.
precondition: Only run challenge when warmup succeeds and a nonempty MEMORY.md was written through the native memory tool. Do not author or correct learned memory. Preserve failed warmups.
memory_transfer: Copy only MEMORY.md to a fresh isolated profile. Fresh MCP discovery avoids confounding stale tool-schema caching with memory persistence.
assessment: Independent world-state ledger, actual model tool calls, actual cached system prompt, and manual final-answer review. No runtime changes. This is a small explicit learning task, not an estimate of naturally occurring production failures.
